title: From theta periods to zeros
guide: The first chapter follows the proof from the choice of prime-counting windows to the functional equation. Subsequent chapters supply its arithmetic and analytic details. Throughout the generalized hypothesis concerns all Dirichlet characters.

title: Constructing a common arithmetic window
guide: The analytic and cohomological estimates must hold for the same choices of auxiliary primes on an interval. We begin with the character group that detects the target, then establish the prime and cohomological estimates with their uniformity in the host field. The final two constructions identify the field, lattices and translations used at each real scale.

title: The theta tower and the comparison of its periods
guide: A divisibility statement for an algebraic map can bound a period only after identifying the two realizations and their normalizations. The base theta construction leads to the arithmetic seesaw, the comparison of fields and tests, and the period on the full reference row.

title: Congruences and finite divisibility
guide: The same lattice is involved in differentiating a theta kernel, cutting out a family of Hecke eigensystems, and taking determinants of the lift. The local arithmetic is established before the valuation bounds are summed with their prime weights.

title: Arithmetic volume and the height of a period
guide: The lower bound for sections is first proved on a geometric cover. Integral tests, comparison of the metrics, descent to the required type and a determinant argument then transfer it to a bound at the actual weight and degree. The functional inequality uses this particular lattice.

title: Estimates for the full period operators
guide: The Hilbert–Schmidt estimates sum over the full source columns. The identity and zero-Gram cells behave differently for equal and unequal words. For unequal words the paired orbits, interpolation on flags, finite densities and the two split primes together determine the leading coefficient.

title: Prime discrepancies and the critical line
guide: Determinant gains are averaged over translations and converted into a statement about a weighted sum of primes. The signed analytic argument detects a pole from that one-sided estimate. The functional equation and the passage from primitive to imprimitive characters finish the deduction.

title: Mathematical sources and the remaining expansions
guide: The guide records the original formal declarations, primary publications, and contributions of other reconstructions. The coverage analysis identifies the dependencies still requiring a purely mathematical derivation in this edition.
